question: The microscopic channels, which traverse the cell walls of plant cells and some algal cells, enabling transport and communication between them is called:
solution:
The correct answer is __**plasmodesmata**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **plasmodesmata:**
 
• Plasmodesmata are microscopic channels that traverse the cell walls of plant cells and some algal cells.
 
• They facilitate the transport of materials, including water, nutrients, and signaling molecules, between adjacent cells.
 
• They are crucial for cell-to-cell communication and coordination within plant tissues.
 
• They allow for the symplastic transport of substances, meaning movement within the continuous cytoplasm of interconnected cells.
 
• They play vital roles in processes like nutrient distribution, signal transduction, and defense responses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ribosomes:**
 
• Ribosomes are cellular organelles responsible for protein synthesis.
 
• They are found in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.
 
• They consist of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and proteins.
 
• They translate genetic information from messenger RNA (mRNA) into polypeptide chains.
 
• They are essential for all living cells to produce the proteins necessary for cellular functions.
 
• **lysosomes:**
 
• Lysosomes are membrane-bound organelles found in animal cells and some plant cells.
 
• They contain hydrolytic enzymes that break down waste materials and cellular debris.
 
• They play a crucial role in intracellular digestion and recycling.
 
• They are involved in processes like autophagy (self-digestion) and apoptosis (programmed cell death).
 
• They help to defend the cell against invading bacteria and viruses.
 
• **desmosomes:**
 
• Desmosomes are cell junctions that provide strong adhesion between animal cells.
 
• They are particularly abundant in tissues that experience mechanical stress, such as skin and muscle.
 
• They consist of proteins that link the cytoskeletons of adjacent cells.
 
• They contribute to the structural integrity and stability of tissues.
 
• They are not found in plant cells, as plant cell walls fulfill a structural role.
